title: Cohomology on a qcqs object commutes with bounded-below filtered colimits
statement:
Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], and use its small pro-étale site $X_{\mathrm{proét}}$ [sk-def-pe-site] in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $\mathcal R$ be a sheaf of rings on this site, and let $U$ be a quasi-compact, quasi-separated object (its underlying scheme has a finite affine open cover, and intersections of affine opens are quasi-compact). Let $I$ be a small filtered category [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit], let $a\in\mathbf Z$, and let $(K_i^\bullet)_{i\in I}$ be a diagram of cochain complexes [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] of sheaves of left $\mathcal R$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], with $K_i^b=0$ for every $i$ and $b<a$. Colimits of these complexes are taken termwise in sheaves of $\mathcal R$-modules. Write $H^q(U,L^\bullet)=H^q(R\Gamma(U,L^\bullet))$ for hypercohomology, where $R\Gamma(U,-)$ is computed by evaluating a bounded-below injective resolution at $U$, with values in complexes of abelian groups. Then for every $q\in\mathbf Z$ the canonical map induced by the colimit cocone is an isomorphism:
$$
\varinjlim_{i\in I}H^q(U,K_i^\bullet)\longrightarrow H^q\bigl(U,\varinjlim_{i\in I}K_i^\bullet\bigr).
$$

proof.text: Choose one affine weakly contractible hypercover W of U using exists_proetale_hypercover_single_affine. Each term is the spectrum of a w-contractible ring; isWeaklyContractible_of_iso supplies weak contractibility in the coefficient universe. The zero and matching covering data are exactly those required by hypercover_complex_natural_iso.

proof.text: Identify the published small-model K-injective definition of ringHypercohomology with homology of the right derived abelian evaluation functor. Construct the equivalence of module-sheaf categories by continuous pushforwards along AsSmall. Transport the functorial K-injective resolution back through this equivalence; the unit is a quasi-isomorphism and its target is K-injective. The right-derived unit on K-injectives and functorial quasi-isomorphism of the resolution give a natural isomorphism. Compose it, on Plus, with hypercover_complex_natural_iso and homologyFunctorFactors to identify hypercohomology naturally with homology of the explicit hypercover total.

proof.text: The forgetful functor from module sheaves to abelian sheaves preserves colimits by moduleSheaves_colimits_forgetful. The module-coefficient hypercover rows are definitionally its composite with abelianHypercoverRows. Apply mapHomologicalComplexCompIso and whisker with flip and total to identify their total functors. The existing abelianHypercoverTotal_preservesColimits theorem now proves colimit preservation of the module-coefficient total. This reuses the sectionwise, alternating-face, extension, and coproduct-total calculations rather than reproving them.

proof.text: Module sheaves have small colimits by the Grothendieck module-sheaf instance. Colimits of complexes are computed degreewise. Below the common bound a, the degreewise colimit has zero identity: test the identity and zero on every colimit leg, whose source is zero. Thus the entire diagram and its colimit cocone lift to Plus. Filtered colimits of abelian groups are exact, so the homology functor preserves these colimits, using HomologicalComplex homology colimit preservation in DegreewiseLimits.

source.place: Whole proof: fixed hypercover, total colimits, exact filtered colimits, and naturality

proof.text: Map the lifted cocone by the hypercover total and homology; it is a colimit by the two preservation results. Transfer its colimit property along the inverse of the natural isomorphism of step 2 using IsColimit.mapCoconeEquiv. Its underlying cocone is exactly the ringHypercohomology image of colimit.cocone K. Hence that functor preserves this colimit, and the canonical colimit.post is an isomorphism. Naturality is incorporated in the cocone transfer, with no separately chosen comparison map. All integer degrees, the zero complexes, and the empty effective diagonals are included.

lean.statement: theorem isIso_ringHypercohomology_colimitPost (X : Scheme.{u}) (R : Sheaf (topology X) RingCat.{u + 1}) (U : X.ProEt) [CompactSpace U.left] [QuasiSeparatedSpace U.left] {I : Type (u + 1)} [SmallCategory I] [IsFiltered I] (K : I ⥤ CochainComplex (ringedSiteModules.{u + 1} R) ℤ) (a : ℤ) (hK : ∀ (i : I) (b : ℤ), b < a → IsZero ((K.obj i).X b)) (q : ℤ) : IsIso (colimit.post K (ringHypercohomology X R U q))
lean.note: The hypercohomology helper is the actual composite of published sectionwise small-site transport, functorial K-injective resolution, abelian evaluation and integer-degree homology. Its named zero-map transport lemma is the structural proof needed to apply transport to complexes. Both are helpers of this node, not alternative coefficient categories or arbitrary comparison maps.
